sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: a ratio of one party's earnings figure to the other party's capital figure, both printed as three-year averages in one submission, measured against a range in the Commission's summary; the exact ratio sits between two printed look-alikes; medium; measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 9 chart figures 283 (the Commission's earnings) and 2,085 (Z's capital employed); 283 / 2,085 = 13.573%; Doc 1 X45.2 range top 8.6%; 13.573 - 8.6 = 4.973 -> 5.0. Form-safe chain: 2,085 x 8.6% = 179.31; 283 - 179.31 = 103.69; 103.69 / 2,085 = 4.973%.
- Universe: not applicable (single value).
- Necessity: Doc 9 is the only document with Z's earnings or capital employed (searched "283", "2,085", "capital employed", "ROACE" in all eleven). Doc 1 is the only document with the range (searched "6.9", "8.6", "WACC", "reasonable return", "fair return"); Doc 10 line 485 "a WACC of 8%" gives 5.6, not 5.0. Without Doc 1 the top of the range is unknown.
- Selected-lever checks: exact table vs rounded prose: Doc 9's prose gives approximately 22% less approximately 9% = 13%, which is 4.4 above the top; the chart figures give 13.57% and 5.0, so the lever changes the answer. Readings that agree: ratio of the averages 13.573% (4.97) and the mean of the three yearly ratios from Appendix 2, 13.458 / 14.793 / 12.685, mean 13.645% (5.04); both 5.0 at one decimal.
- Targeted failure modes: Look-alike measure, recomputed: 14 - 8.6 = 5.4 (D11 line 220, "a materially lower ROACE of 14%"). Considered and not declared before a run shows which routes solvers take: the prose route 22 - 9 - 8.6 = 4.4; reading "by approximately 9%" as a relative cut, 22 x 0.91 = 20.0, 11.4 above; Z's own pair 231 / 2,085 = 11.08%, 2.5 above; the Commission's own pair 283 / 1,254 = 22.57%, 14.0 above; the bottom of the range, 6.7 above.
- Calculation verification: python, 2026-10-12 (caller, and the independent author by exact fractions): 283 / 2,085 = 0.135731; 2,085 x 0.086 = 179.31; 283 - 179.31 = 103.69; 103.69 / 2,085 = 0.049731. Rounding the ROACE first (13.6 - 8.6) gives 5.0 as well.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: "13.5", "13.6" and a 5.0 excess are printed nowhere; the nearest printed figure is 14%. Bundle overview lists the 22% and 11.3% only. Shortest complete route: two chart figures and Doc 1's range.
- Precision/readings: capital employed 2,085 or the appendix mean 2,085.17: 5.0 either way. "Earnings" is the chart's own word for the after-tax figure (283).
- Completeness: no source gaps; all eleven documents read in full.

sections.question: Z Energy says the Commission left components out of its capital employed. Keeping the Commission's 2016 to 2018 average earnings for Z but using Z's own average capital employed, by how many percentage points would Z's ROACE exceed the top of the Commission's reasonable-return range? Give one decimal place.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 9, the chart of 2016 to 2018 average earnings): the Commission's assessment of Z Energy's earnings is 283, in $ million a year. Z's own assessment in the same chart is 231, which the question sets aside.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 9, the chart of 2016 to 2018 average capital employed): Z's own assessment of its capital employed is 2,085, in $ million. The Commission's assessment in the same chart is 1,254, which the question sets aside.

Step 3. Check (Doc 9): the two Commission figures are a pair, because their ratio is the ROACE that Doc 9 reports for the Commission's approach, approximately 22%: 283 / 1,254 = 22.6%

Step 4. Source input (Doc 9, paragraph 26): Z says that including the components the Commission left out of capital employed would reduce its ROACE on the Commission's numbers by approximately 9%. That is the case the question describes: the Commission's earnings over Z's capital employed. Doc 9 gives the size of the fall only as an approximation, so the ratio is worked out from the two chart figures.

Step 5. Calculation (Doc 9): Z's ROACE on that basis: 283 / 2,085 = 13.6%

Step 6. Source input (Doc 1, paragraph X45.2): the Commission's estimate of a reasonable return is the range 6.9 - 8.6%, so the top of the range is 8.6%.

Step 7. Calculation (Doc 9 and Doc 1): the yearly earnings, in $ million, that a return at the top of the range gives on Z's figure for capital employed: 2,085 × 8.6% = 179.31

Step 8. Calculation (Doc 9 and Doc 1): the part of the Commission's earnings figure above that return, in $ million a year: 283 − 179.31 = 103.69

Step 9. Final answer (Doc 9 and Doc 1): that part as a rate on Z's capital employed, which is the number of percentage points by which the ROACE exceeds the top of the range, to one decimal place: 103.69 / 2,085 = 5.0%
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Look-alike measure
How a careless solver fails: Takes the wrong line item

Why these are traps: Look-alike measure: Doc 9's paragraph 49 prints a 14% ROACE for Z, the Commission's comparator-group figure, close to the case asked about. Taking it gives 5.4. The question names the Commission's earnings (283) and Z's capital employed (2,085), whose ratio is 13.57%, so the answer is 5.0.
